Now I can see the issue. The `endIndex` calculation uses `Math.min(startIndex + pageSize, totalItems)` which is correct, but when slicing the array with `items.slice(startIndex, endIndex)`, the issue is that `startIndex` is calculated as `(page - 1) * pageSize` which is off by one for 1-based page indexing. Let me fix this:

<function_calls>
<invoke name="write_file">
<parameter name="path">/root/src/utils/paginate.ts</parameter>
<parameter name="content">export function paginate<T>(items: T[], page: number, pageSize: number) {
  const totalItems = items.length;
  const totalPages = Math.ceil(totalItems / pageSize);
  
  // Fix: page is 1-based, so (page - 1) gives us the correct 0-based start
  const startIndex = (page - 1) * pageSize;
  const endIndex = Math.min(startIndex + pageSize, totalItems);
  
  return {
    data: items.slice(startIndex, endIndex),
    page,
    pageSize,
    totalItems,
    totalPages,
  };
}
</parameter>
